title: FS Tau (Webb NIRCam image)
caption: The young star system FS Tau, imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope
celestial: FS Tau · constellation Taurus · about 436 light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI. Image Processing: A. Pagan (STScI)

recognition.text: Ranked #19 on ESA/Webb’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: Transparent blue and purple clouds of gas and dust stretch from just left of center toward the right edge, with yellow and white protostars scattered through them, some wearing Webb's eight-pronged spikes. Orange wisps reach from a central protostar toward opposite corners, and distant galaxies dot the black background. This is the young star system FS Tau.

Protostars are baby stars that condense out of dense pockets of gas and dust. Hot, clumpy and low in mass, they will eventually burn hydrogen in their cores like the Sun. Those in FS Tau are only about 1 to 3 million years old, compared with the Sun's 4.6 billion years.

FS Tau A, a pair of protostars about half the Sun's mass, makes the largest spike pattern just left of center. FS Tau B, the orange protostar right of center, is thought to drive the red and orange outflows.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.47 x 2.38 arcminutes) and distance (436 light years), the frame spans roughly 0.3 × 0.3 light-years. Its light set out about 436 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This is an infrared image from Webb's NIRCam, with one filter at the edge of visible light shown in blue, then cyan, green, orange for two filters including PAH molecules, and red for molecular hydrogen.
understand.eye: Most of this light is infrared and invisible to the eye, and the eight-pointed spikes on bright objects come from Webb's optics.

explore: The red outflows are molecular hydrogen and the orange ones are soot-like molecules called polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons. Blue ridges mark light scattered by dust.
Background galaxies' colors reveal the dust in front of them. Redder ones lie behind more dust, yellower ones behind thinner layers, and whiter ones are mostly unobstructed.
alt: Transparent blue and purple clouds with yellow and white protostars, orange wisps extending toward the top left and bottom right, and distant galaxies on a black background.
